1	# Architecture
2	
3	|              |                                                                                                      |
4	| ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
5	| Status       | Proposed. It becomes the baseline when the ADRs it cites are accepted                                |
6	| Date         | 2 November 2026                                                                                      |
7	| Requirements | Discovery package v0.1, mainly T2, T3 and T4. Digest: [discovery-baseline.md](discovery-baseline.md) |
8	| Decisions    | [adr/](adr/README.md)                                                                                |
9	
10	This document describes the target architecture of the platform: the shop with the customer account, the advisor portal, the head office portal and the background work. It explains how the design meets the package. The ADRs hold the reasons and the alternatives.
11	
12	## 1. Drivers
13	
14	| Driver                                                  | Source                               | Consequence for the design                                                                     |
15	| ------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
16	| The ERP leads most data; the platform holds copies      | DP1, T1 section 2                    | A small commerce core of our own; read copies with source and age; no commerce engine          |
17	| One port to the ERP, two adapters over time             | T3-D-005, T2-D-001                   | ERP access only through the integration module; contract-first payloads                        |
18	| Provider-neutral hosting                                | T3-D-006, T3-O-001                   | Containers, PostgreSQL, an S3-compatible store, a queue on PostgreSQL; no single-cloud service |
19	| Short time to RC                                        | DR section 2                         | A modular monolith in one repository; one database; few moving parts                           |
20	| Settings without a release                              | DR section 8                         | Rule sets as versioned data                                                                    |
21	| Personal data rules and EU-only production access       | T3 section 5, T4 section 4, T4-O-002 | Field metadata, masked telemetry, deployments through Git                                      |
22	| Blue-green release, 99.5 % availability, RPO 15 minutes | T4 sections 2 and 5                  | Rolling blue-green on Kubernetes; managed PostgreSQL with point-in-time recovery               |
23	
24	## 2. Context
25	
26	```mermaid
27	flowchart LR
28	  customer["Customer"] --> shop
29	  advisor["Advisor"] --> shop
30	  advisor --> portal
31	  staff["Head office staff"] --> office
32	  subgraph platform["Platform"]
33	    shop["Shop and account"]
34	    portal["Advisor portal"]
35	    office["Head office portal"]
36	    back["Worker and integration gateway"]
37	  end
38	  back <--> erp["ERP: NAV 2015, later Business Central"]
39	  shop <--> psp["Stripe and PayPal"]
40	  back --> mail["E-mail delivery service"]
41	  back --> mkt["Inxmail"]
42	  back <--> ticket["Ticket tool"]
43	  back --> ai["AI provider"]
44	  shop --> addr["Address validation"]
45	  back --> carrier["Carrier return service"]
46	  office --> idp["Company directory"]
47	  shop --> analytics["Web analytics, with consent"]
48	```
49	
50	The current shop runs next to the platform from RC to the cutover. No interface writes into the current shop (T1 section 3.1).
51	
52	## 3. Runtime units
53	
54	All units come from one repository and one build. See ADR-0003.
55	
56	| Unit                  | Rendering       | Exposure                                                | Scaling                                   | Purpose                                                                                                        |
57	| --------------------- | --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
58	| `shop`                | Server-rendered | Public, main domain, behind the edge                    | Horizontal; carries the launch peak       | Catalogue, advisor path and page, cart, checkout, customer account, content pages, redirects, payment webhooks |
59	| `portal`              | Client-rendered | Public, own subdomain                                   | Horizontal                                | Advisor portal: customers, leads, tasks, figures, statements, own page, e-mail to a customer                   |
60	| `head-office`         | Client-rendered | Own subdomain, restricted at the edge                   | 1 to 2 replicas                           | Head office portal (A4-C-020)                                                                                  |
61	| `worker`              | —               | None                                                    | 1 or more; separate queues for heavy work | Scheduled and queued jobs (T3-D-003)                                                                           |
62	| `integration-gateway` | —               | Internal only, plus an allow-listed path for ERP pushes | 2 replicas                                | The only network path to the ERP: synchronous reads for the checkout, inbound ERP exports                      |
63	
64	```mermaid
65	flowchart TB
66	  edge["Edge: CDN, WAF, bot protection, redirects"] --> shop & portal & office
67	  shop["shop"] --> db[("PostgreSQL")]
68	  portal["portal"] --> db
69	  office["head-office"] --> db
70	  worker["worker"] --> db
71	  gw["integration-gateway"] --> db
72	  shop -- "3 sync reads, short timeout" --> gw
73	  worker -- "outbound flows through the port" --> gw
74	  gw -- "one encrypted connection" --> erp["ERP"]
75	  erp -- "scheduled exports" --> gw
76	  shop & portal & office & worker --> store[("Object store")]
77	  store --> edge
78	```
79	
80	**Why a gateway.** T3-D-005 allows ERP access only through the integration module. T2-D-008 asks for one authenticated, encrypted connection. Three reads must be synchronous at the checkout (payment options, the live voucher read, the order history). The integration gateway gives one network identity, one set of ERP credentials and one egress path. The NAV adapter runs only in this unit. See ADR-0006.
81	
82	**Note on T3.** T3 section 3 explains "one application image, one worker image". This design builds one image per web app and one image for the worker and the gateway. T3 allows this change if the acceptance criteria and the T4 values hold (T3 section 3). ADR-0003 records it.
83	
84	## 4. Modules
85	
86	The domain code lives in `packages/core`. It has no dependency on the web framework. Each module owns its PostgreSQL schema and exposes a public API through its `index.ts`. A module never reads another module's tables.
87	
88	| Module         | Owns                                                                                                        | Reads from the ERP (through `integration`)                                     | Emits events                                     |
89	| -------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------ |
90	| `identity`     | Person, roles with dates, credentials, sessions, staff accounts, consents, preferences, pets, consultations | Customer and advisor master data, assignment                                   | Person registered, consent changed, role started |
91	| `commerce`     | Catalogue view, cart, checkout, payments, voucher redemption, calculators, orders until the hand-off        | Prices, campaigns, vouchers, fees, stock, payment options                      | Order placed, payment captured, order accepted   |
92	| `subscription` | Subscriptions, schedules, due-delivery run, holds, self-service, charge at shipment                         | Shipment report, payment options                                               | Delivery due, delivery charged                   |
93	| `commission`   | Periods, points, levels, runs, statements, comparison, commission settings                                  | Point values, corrections, structure, assignment, invoice status, NAV's result | Run released                                     |
94	| `journey`      | Events, journeys, tasks, leads, messages, advisor e-mails                                                   | Order, invoice and payment events                                              | Task created, message sent                       |
95	| `content`      | Pages, product texts, media and variants, advisor pages, moderation                                         | —                                                                              | Content published                                |

# Architecture

|              |                                                                                                      |
| ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Status       | Proposed. It becomes the baseline when the ADRs it cites are accepted                                |
| Date         | 2 November 2026                                                                                      |
| Requirements | Discovery package v0.1, mainly T2, T3 and T4. Digest: [discovery-baseline.md](discovery-baseline.md) |
| Decisions    | [adr/](adr/README.md)                                                                                |

This document describes the target architecture of the platform: the shop with the customer account, the advisor portal, the head office portal and the background work. It explains how the design meets the package. The ADRs hold the reasons and the alternatives.

## 1. Drivers

| Driver                                                  | Source                               | Consequence for the design                                                                     |
| ------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| The ERP leads most data; the platform holds copies      | DP1, T1 section 2                    | A small commerce core of our own; read copies with source and age; no commerce engine          |
| One port to the ERP, two adapters over time             | T3-D-005, T2-D-001                   | ERP access only through the integration module; contract-first payloads                        |
| Provider-neutral hosting                                | T3-D-006, T3-O-001                   | Containers, PostgreSQL, an S3-compatible store, a queue on PostgreSQL; no single-cloud service |
| Short time to RC                                        | DR section 2                         | A modular monolith in one repository; one database; few moving parts                           |
| Settings without a release                              | DR section 8                         | Rule sets as versioned data                                                                    |
| Personal data rules and EU-only production access       | T3 section 5, T4 section 4, T4-O-002 | Field metadata, masked telemetry, deployments through Git                                      |
| Blue-green release, 99.5 % availability, RPO 15 minutes | T4 sections 2 and 5                  | Rolling blue-green on Kubernetes; managed PostgreSQL with point-in-time recovery               |

## 2. Context

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  customer["Customer"] --> shop
  advisor["Advisor"] --> shop
  advisor --> portal
  staff["Head office staff"] --> office
  subgraph platform["Platform"]
    shop["Shop and account"]
    portal["Advisor portal"]
    office["Head office portal"]
    back["Worker and integration gateway"]
  end
  back <--> erp["ERP: NAV 2015, later Business Central"]
  shop <--> psp["Stripe and PayPal"]
  back --> mail["E-mail delivery service"]
  back --> mkt["Inxmail"]
  back <--> ticket["Ticket tool"]
  back --> ai["AI provider"]
  shop --> addr["Address validation"]
  back --> carrier["Carrier return service"]
  office --> idp["Company directory"]
  shop --> analytics["Web analytics, with consent"]
```

The current shop runs next to the platform from RC to the cutover. No interface writes into the current shop (T1 section 3.1).

## 3. Runtime units

All units come from one repository and one build. See ADR-0003.

| Unit                  | Rendering       | Exposure                                                | Scaling                                   | Purpose                                                                                                        |
| --------------------- | --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `shop`                | Server-rendered | Public, main domain, behind the edge                    | Horizontal; carries the launch peak       | Catalogue, advisor path and page, cart, checkout, customer account, content pages, redirects, payment webhooks |
| `portal`              | Client-rendered | Public, own subdomain                                   | Horizontal                                | Advisor portal: customers, leads, tasks, figures, statements, own page, e-mail to a customer                   |
| `head-office`         | Client-rendered | Own subdomain, restricted at the edge                   | 1 to 2 replicas                           | Head office portal (A4-C-020)                                                                                  |
| `worker`              | —               | None                                                    | 1 or more; separate queues for heavy work | Scheduled and queued jobs (T3-D-003)                                                                           |
| `integration-gateway` | —               | Internal only, plus an allow-listed path for ERP pushes | 2 replicas                                | The only network path to the ERP: synchronous reads for the checkout, inbound ERP exports                      |

```mermaid
flowchart TB

  shop["shop"] --> db[("PostgreSQL")]
  portal["portal"] --> db
  office["head-office"] --> db
  worker["worker"] --> db
  gw["integration-gateway"] --> db
  shop -- "3 sync reads, short timeout" --> gw
  worker -- "outbound flows through the port" --> gw
  gw -- "one encrypted connection" --> erp["ERP"]
```

**Why a gateway.** T3-D-005 allows ERP access only through the integration module. T2-D-008 asks for one authenticated, encrypted connection. Three reads must be synchronous at the checkout (payment options, the live voucher read, the order history). The integration gateway gives one network identity, one set of ERP credentials and one egress path. The NAV adapter runs only in this unit. See ADR-0006.

**Note on T3.** T3 section 3 explains "one application image, one worker image". This design builds one image per web app and one image for the worker and the gateway. T3 allows this change if the acceptance criteria and the T4 values hold (T3 section 3). ADR-0003 records it.

## 4. Modules

The domain code lives in `packages/core`. It has no dependency on the web framework. Each module owns its PostgreSQL schema and exposes a public API through its `index.ts`. A module never reads another module's tables.

| `content`      | Pages, product texts, media and variants, advisor pages, moderation                                         | —                                                                              | Content published                                |
| `ai`           | The AI gateway: prompt, limit, record and off switch per function (T3-D-010)                                | —                                                                              | —                                                |
